questions.text: The Battle of Plassey, a decisive victory for the British East India Company over the Nawab of Bengal Siraj-ud-Daulah, was fought in which year?
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: Use the '57' mnemonic — Plassey (1757) and Revolt (1857) both end in '57'. Buxar (1764) ends in '64'. Eliminate 1764 (Buxar), 1748 (too early), and 1775 (too late). Full Solution: The Battle of Plassey was fought on 23 June 1757 near the Bhagirathi River. Robert Clive led the Company forces against Nawab Siraj-ud-Daulah, marking the beginning of British political control in India.

questions.text: According to Article 85(1) of the Constitution of India, what is the maximum permissible gap between the last sitting of one session of Parliament and the first sitting of the next session?
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: Remember the universal 'Six Month' rule in Polity: Gap between Parliament sessions (Art 85), President's Rule duration (Art 356), Ordinance validity (Art 123/213), and Money Bill reconsideration (Art 110) — all are capped at six months. Full Solution: Article 85(1) mandates that the President shall summon each House of Parliament at such intervals that six months shall not intervene between its last sitting in one session and the date appointed for its first sitting in the next session.

questions.text: The HCF of two numbers is 12 and their LCM is 360. If one number is 60, find the other number.
questions.solution: Shortcut: Product of two numbers = HCF × LCM. So the other number = (12 × 360) / 60 = 72. Full: Let the numbers be 60 and x. Then 60 × x = 12 × 360 => x = (12 × 360)/60 = 72.

questions.text: The Standard Meridian of India, passing through Mirzapur (Uttar Pradesh), determines the Indian Standard Time (IST). What is its longitudinal value?
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: IST is UTC+5:30. Since 1 hour = 15° longitude, 5.5 hours × 15° = 82.5° East. Eliminate West longitudes (C) and values not matching 82.5° (A, D). Full Solution: The 82°30' East meridian (82.5°E) passing through Mirzapur, Uttar Pradesh, is the Standard Meridian of India. It sets Indian Standard Time (IST) which is 5 hours 30 minutes ahead of Greenwich Mean Time (GMT/UTC).

questions.text: Find the next term in the series: 2, 6, 12, 20, 30, ?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognize the series as n × (n+1) for n = 1,2,3…; the 6th term is 6×7 = 42. Step-by-step: Differences are 4,6,8,10 (increasing by 2), so next difference is 12, giving 30+12 = 42.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CAT' is written as 'DBU'. How will 'DOG' be written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Each letter in the code is the immediate next letter in the alphabet (C→D, A→B, T→U). Apply the same +1 shift to DOG: D→E, O→P, G→H, giving EPH. Full solution: Compare CAT and DBU; the pattern is a consistent forward shift of one position. Using this rule on DOG yields EPH, which matches option C.

questions.text: A certain sum amounts to ₹ 5,600 in 3 years and ₹ 6,800 in 6 years at simple interest. What is the principal?
questions.solution: Shortcut: The difference in amounts (₹6,800−₹5,600=₹1,200) is the interest for 3 years (6−3), so annual interest = ₹400. Interest for 3 years = ₹1,200, thus principal = ₹5,600−₹1,200 = ₹4,400. Full: Let P be principal, R rate. Amount after 3 years = P+3PR/100 = 5600; after 6 years = P+6PR/100 = 6800. Subtracting gives 3PR/100 = 1200 => PR/100 = 400. Substitute back: P+3*400 = 5600 => P = 4400.

questions.text: In a certain code language, 'CAT' is written as '27' and 'DOG' is written as '29'. How will 'RAT' be written in that code?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Code = Sum of alphabetical positions of letters + Number of letters. CAT: 3+1+20+3=27. DOG: 4+15+7+3=29. RAT: 18+1+20+3=42. Step-by-step: Verify pattern with given words. C(3)+A(1)+T(20)=24, +3 letters=27. D(4)+O(15)+G(7)=26, +3 letters=29. Apply to RAT: R(18)+A(1)+T(20)=39, +3 letters=42.

questions.text: Identify the segment in the sentence which contains a grammatical error. If there is no error, select 'No error'. The quality of the mangoes grown in this orchard / are superior to those / grown in the neighbouring farms / No error

options.label: A
options.text: The quality of the mangoes grown in this orchard

questions.solution: Shortcut: Apply the Subject-Verb Agreement rule: The verb agrees with the Main Subject, not the noun in the intervening 'of' phrase. Main Subject = 'The quality' (Singular). Verb 'are' is Plural -> Error. Correction: 'is superior'. Step-by-step: Locate the true subject 'The quality'. Ignore the prepositional phrase 'of the mangoes...'. Singular subject requires singular verb 'is'. Segment B uses plural verb 'are', creating a disagreement. Hence error lies in Segment B.

questions.text: Choose the correct passive form of the given sentence. The railway authorities have announced a new timetable for the festive season.

options.label: A
options.text: A new timetable for the festive season has been announced by the railway authorities.

options.label: B
options.text: A new timetable for the festive season have been announced by the railway authorities.

options.label: C
options.text: A new timetable for the festive season was announced by the railway authorities.

options.label: D
options.text: A new timetable for the festive season is announced by the railway authorities.

questions.solution: Shortcut: Identify the tense of the active verb ('have announced' = Present Perfect). Passive structure for Present Perfect is 'has/have been + V3'. The new subject 'A new timetable' is singular, so select 'has been'. Option A matches. Step-by-step: Active Subject (Authorities) + have announced (Pres Perf) + Object (Timetable). Passive: Object becomes Subject (Timetable - Singular) + has been + V3 (announced) + by + Agent. 'Have' changes to 'Has' for singular subject.

questions.text: Choose the word that best substitutes the given group of words. One who walks on foot / A person who travels on foot
questions.solution: Shortcut: Recognize the root 'Ped/Pedis' (Latin for foot). 'Pedestrian' directly means a walker on foot. Eliminate 'Pediatrician' (child doctor, Greek 'pais'), 'Pedagogue' (teacher, Greek 'pais'), and 'Pedometer' (step measuring device, 'meter'). Step-by-step: Analyze etymology. Pedestrian < Latin pedester (on foot). Pediatrician < Greek pais (child). Pedagogue < Greek paidagogos (child leader). Pedometer < French pedometre (foot measure). Only Option A fits the definition.

questions.text: In a certain code language, each letter is replaced by its reverse alphabetical counterpart (A↔Z, B↔Y, C↔X, …). What is the code for the word 'MATH'?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Use the Atbash cipher – the position of a letter from start equals the position of its code from end (1↔26, 2↔25, …). Step-by-step: M(13)→N(14), A(1)→Z(26), T(20)→G(7), H(8)→S(19), giving NZGS.

questions.text: The radius of a circle is increased by 50%. What is the percentage increase in its area?
questions.solution: Shortcut: Area ∝ r². New radius = 1.5r, so new area = (1.5)² = 2.25 times original, i.e., a 125% increase. Full: Original area = πr². New area = π(1.5r)² = 2.25πr². Increase = 2.25πr² − πr² = 1.25πr², which is 125% of original.

questions.text: Which inert gas is most commonly filled in modern incandescent electric bulbs to reduce the evaporation of the tungsten filament and prevent its oxidation?
questions.solution: Shortcut/Trick: Eliminate by application: Neon (glow sign tubes), Helium (balloons, light, escapes), Krypton (expensive, specialized lamps). Argon is cheap, abundant (~1% air), heavy, and inert — ideal for mass-produced bulbs. Full Solution: Argon (often mixed with nitrogen) is used because it is chemically inert, inexpensive, and its higher atomic weight reduces the rate of tungsten filament evaporation compared to vacuum or lighter gases, significantly increasing bulb life.

questions.text: A man travels from point A to point B at a speed of 40 km/h and returns from B to A at a speed of 60 km/h. What is his average speed for the entire round trip?
questions.solution: Shortcut: For equal distances, average speed = 2ab/(a+b) = 2×40×60/(40+60) = 4800/100 = 48 km/h. Full method: Let distance be d km. Time for onward = d/40 h, return = d/60 h. Total distance = 2d, total time = d/40 + d/60 = (3d+2d)/120 = 5d/120 = d/24 h. Average speed = 2d ÷ (d/24) = 48 km/h.
